correctness.rationale: For every clade the probability of being represented is one minus its exact hypergeometric absence probability, and its successive mass increments decrease. Integration across equal-height tree cuts proves the star direction. A direct two-draw pairwise-patristic formula and a penultimate-draw singleton-branch identity establish a negative-then-positive transfer on every nonstar tree. Exhausting legal transfers and every possible horizontal cut for N<=5 proves impossibility there. An exact three-tip N=6 example shows attainability; its affine six-depth differences were independently verified by full enumeration. Distinct finite checks corroborate rather than substitute for the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: Abundance balancing is central to ecological evenness assessment; sampled species richness is transfer-monotone, but this theorem proves phylogenetic diversity can instead lose expected evolutionary history at shallow sampling. The exact star iff criterion, every-nonstar existence of opposite sampling-depth effects, and sharp minimum N=6 jointly provide a useful structural boundary for whether an abundance-evenness interpretation transfers to phylogenetic rarefaction. The result neither depends on an arbitrary numerical slice nor claims ecological causality. The limited tree and sampling scope is explicitly stated.
